workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§151–153
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§151–153: Wang Qan's flight, and the law before the Tatar battle
part: §§151–153 — Wang Qan's flight, and the law before the Tatar battle
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§151–153, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Wang Qan, Chinggis's old ally, is hunted by his own brother, runs to the Naiman and the Qara-Kitad (the Black Khitan), and comes back starving; Chinggis takes him in. His brothers plot against him and one of the plotters tells Wang Qan, who spits in their faces. Then comes the autumn war with the Tatars, and the rule Chinggis lays down before the fight: no stopping for plunder until the enemy is beaten.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoina Waṅ-Qān-(n)u deġü Erke-Qara Waṅ-Qān aqa-daγ̇an alaγdarun buruγ̇udču odču Naiman-u Inanča Qān-dur orožuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: that, he, she (stem teġün- before case endings) [那的]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名的]
genitive: of (back-vowel form; the bracketed (n) is Shiratori's, the stem already ending in n)

words.reading: 額舌兒客-中合舌剌 Erke-Qara

morph.gloss: Erke-Qara, a man's name (Wang Qan's younger brother) [人名]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
dative-locative, here marking by whom the killing was done
to hide, flee, take cover (stem uncertain) [逃躱着]
Inancha, a name or title (here of the Naiman ruler) [人名]

sentences.l: Of that, after: Waṅ-Qān's younger brother Erke-Qara, Waṅ-Qān, by elder-brother-his, at being killed, fleeing, going, of the Naiman Inanča Qān to, went in.
sentences.i: After that, Wang Qan's younger brother Erke-Qara, when he was about to be killed by his elder brother Wang Qan, fled and went in to Inancha Qan of the Naiman.
sentences.n: -da-γ̇an on aqa is a dative-locative plus the reflexive 'his own'; the Ming gloss 兄 自的行 reads it as 'by his own elder brother', so the dative here names who does the killing. alaγdarun is ala- 'kill' + passive + 'when', so the killing is either done or only threatened — the text does not say which, and 'was about to be killed' is the safer reading of a man who then ran. Erke-Qara and the two Wang Qans are named one after another with no verb between; the sentence only resolves at the end with orožuγ̇ui.

sentences.t: Inanča Qān čeriġüd iležü

morph.gloss: Inancha, a name or title [人名]

sentences.l: Inanča Qān, soldiers, sending,
sentences.i: Inancha Qan sent soldiers,
sentences.n: A short unit cut out of a longer chain: iležü is the -žü converb, glossed by the Ming as 敎去着 'causing to go', so it means 'dispatching'. Note čeriġüd, 'soldiers': čerig with the plural -d and Shiratori's linking -ü-, as the house glossary reads it.

sentences.t: žiči Waṅ-Qān γurban balaγad bitun jorčižu Qara-Kitad-un Gür Qān-dur oduγsan ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: town, city (itself a plural in -d) [城子每]
to go along, skirt (stem uncertain; Ming 沼 'marsh' here, 沿着 'going along' at §152, probably a misprint) [沼]
the Black Khitan (Qara-Kitad), a people [種(名)的]
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
Gür, a title (Gür Qan; Mongol meaning unclear) [人名]
past participle (linking u after a consonant, back-vowel form): who had gone
past tense: was, there was (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Then Waṅ-Qān, three towns, along, going, of the Qara-Kitad to Gür Qān, having gone, he was.
sentences.i: Wang Qan, for his part, passing along three towns, had gone to Gür Qan of the Qara-Kitad.
sentences.n: žiči, glossed 郤 'but, then', turns the story from Inancha to Wang Qan. bitun is doubtful: the Ming has 沼 'marsh', which does not fit; at §152 the same stem is glossed 沿着 'going along', and 沼 is very likely a misprint of 沿 here too. I follow 'going along' but it is a guess. oduγsan ažuγ̇u is a participle plus 'was': a pluperfect, 'had gone'. Gür Qan is the ruler of the Qara-Kitad (Western Liao); Gür itself is only 人名 'a name' in the Ming.

sentences.t: Tendēče bulγa bolun Uiγud-un Taṅγud-un balaγad daγ̇ariγ̇ad

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
to pass by, go past [經過了]

sentences.l: From there, rebellion becoming, of the Uighurs, of the Tangut towns, passing by,
sentences.i: From there, in revolt, he passed by the towns of the Uighurs and the Tangut,
sentences.n: The genitives are a pair — 'the Uighurs' and 'the Tangut' each stand before balaγad 'towns' — with the plural in -d that the Ming marks with 每. bulγa bolun, literally 'becoming a revolt', follows the Ming 反 做着 'doing rebellion'. The text does not say whom Wang Qan revolted against, so the English says only 'in revolt'.

sentences.t: tabun imaγ̇ad širgüġeležü saγ̇al- dužu temeġen-ü čisun qanažu ideġed

morph.gloss: to hold fast, keep confined (stem uncertain) [拘着]
first part of the reciprocal -ldu-, whose -du- opens the next token
-du-: second part of the reciprocal -ldu- (the l is on saγ̇al-): together
to pierce, prick (stem inferred from the Ming 刺着) [刺着]

sentences.l: Five goats, holding fast, milking together, of the camel blood piercing, eating,
sentences.i: holding five goats fast and milking them, pricking a camel's blood and drinking it,
sentences.n: A converb chain in -žu / -žü / -ġed ('-ing'): four links here (širgüġeležü, saγ̇al-dužu, qanažu, ideġed) and a fifth, jadažu, in the next unit; it ends only at ireġesü. The animal imaγan is read from the Ming 𦍩䍽, a rare character for sheep or goats; I say 'goats' without confidence. Bleeding a living camel and drinking the blood is a famine food, as the next unit's 'in want' confirms. saγ̇al-dužu is one word broken across the line: saγa- 'milk' + the reciprocal -ldu- (its l ends the first token) + -žu, 'milking together' (the Ming 共擠); the reciprocal hardly changes the sense.

sentences.t: jadažu Küseġür naγ̇ur-a ireġesü

morph.gloss: to be in want, to lack [貧乏着]
Küseġür, a lake (Ming 海子名) [海︀子名]

sentences.l: Being in want, Küseġür lake at, when he came,
sentences.i: and, in want, when he came to the lake Küsegür,
sentences.n: jadažu is 'being in need'. Küseġür is glossed 海子名 'the name of a lake'; the Ming word 海子, 'sea-child', is the ordinary Chinese rendering of a Mongol lake. Ending in -ġesü (conditional: 'when, if'), the clause is left hanging until the next unit.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan uridu Jesügei Qān- luγ̇a anda keġeldügsen josu-γ̇ar

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Yesügei, Chinggis's father, a man's name [人名]
ruler, khan (the hyphen shows the word runs on into the next token) [皇帝]
comitative: together with (written after a hyphen; Ming 同 'with') [同]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, formerly with Jesügei Qān sworn-brother of the saying, by the custom,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, by the right of the sworn brotherhood that had formerly been declared with Yesügei Qan,
sentences.n: keġeldügsen is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- + the participle -gsen: 'that had said to one another', here 'that had mutually declared' — the declaration being 'we are anda'. The text names only one party, Yesügei, and no subject for the declaring. Yesügei is Chinggis's father, so Chinggis cannot be the other party; the previous part (§150) tells of the anda-bond between Yesügei and Wang Qan, and that is the bond meant. The English leaves the second party unnamed rather than supply it. josu-γ̇ar, 'by the custom, in the right way', is the Ming 理 依着. Qān- and luγ̇a are one word cut at the line break (Qān-luγ̇a, 'with the Qan'): the hyphen is the printer's, not a name.

sentences.t: Taγai-Baγ̇atur, Sükegei-Žeġün qojar-i elči ileġed

words.reading: 塔中孩-把阿禿舌兒 Taγai-Baγ̇atur

morph.gloss: Taqai-Ba'atur, a man's name (Taγai + baγ̇atur 'hero'; Ming 人名 勇士) [人名 勇士]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.l: Taγai-Baγ̇atur, Sükegei-Žeġün, the two, as envoys, sending,
sentences.i: sent as envoys the two men, Taqai-Ba'atur and Sükegei-Jegün.
sentences.n: qojar-i is 'two' in the accusative, with the Ming 兩箇行: 'the two persons', and it governs both names. The Ming marks Taγai with 勇士 'brave warrior' for baγ̇atur, the title that sits inside the name. ileġed (ile- 'send' + -ġed) is the converb that closes the clause begun at Čiṅgis Qaγan in the previous unit; the cut falls here only to keep the units short.

sentences.t: Kelüren-ü teriġün-eče Čiṅgis Qaγan öġesün esergü odču öleščü turužu irebe keġen

morph.gloss: the Kelüren, a river (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
to grow thin, lean (stem inferred from the Ming 瘦) [瘦着]

sentences.l: The Kelüren's source from, Čiṅgis Qaγan himself to meet, going, hungry, gaunt, he has come, saying,
sentences.i: From the source of the Kerülen Chinggis Qahan went out himself to meet him, saying, 'He has come hungry and gaunt.'
sentences.n: keġen, 'saying', closes a quotation in Mongol the way a quotation mark closes it in English, and Shiratori supplies no marks; I have added them in the English only. öġesün esergü is 'himself, to meet' (the Ming 自己 迎着). The ablative -eče on teriġün is odd: 'from the source of the Kelüren' should describe where Chinggis starts out or where the envoys came from, and the Ming does not settle it. I keep 'from', as in the -eče ablative elsewhere; the Ming 處 'place' would also allow 'at', so the place of the meeting is not settled.

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān-(n)a qubčir-i qubčižu ögčü küreġen dotora oroγ̇ulžu težiġebe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to, at (back-vowel form; the bracketed (n) is Shiratori's, the stem already ending in n)
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to levy, gather in (Ming 歛) [歛着]
to rear, bring up, feed [養子]

sentences.l: To Waṅ-Qān, a levy levying, giving, the camp-circle within, bringing in, he reared.
sentences.i: He collected a levy and gave it to Wang Qan, brought him inside the ring of tents, and fed him.
sentences.n: qubčir is glossed 科歛 'a levy, taxing', and the verb qubči- the same, so the sense is that Chinggis raised contributions from his own people to supply Wang Qan. oroγ̇ulžu is oro- 'enter' + causative -γ̇ul- + converb: 'making enter'. Notice -(n)a on Waṅ-Qān, the dative, rendered 行 in the Ming: a recipient. težiġebe, 'reared', is the same verb used elsewhere for bringing up a child.

sentences.t: Tere übül žerge-ġer neġüžü Čiṅgis Qaγan Qubaqaja-ji übülžebe.

morph.gloss: rank, order (Ming 依次 'in turn') [依 次]
to move camp, to migrate [起着]
Qubaqaja, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.l: That winter, by rank, moving camp, Čiṅgis Qaγan Qubaqaja wintered.
sentences.i: That winter Chinggis Qahan moved camp in due order and spent the winter at Qubaqaja.
sentences.n: žerge-ġer, the Ming 依次, 'in order, in turn' — literally 'by rank' — means the camp moved in its proper order. The place Qubaqaja takes an accusative, -ji, as the object of 'wintered', and the Ming 行 marks it. übülžebe is the noun übül 'winter' made into a verb: 'winter-ed'.

sentences.t: Tende Waṅ-Qān-(n)u deġü-ner nojad kiġed ügüleldürün:

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form; the bracketed (n) is Shiratori's, the stem already ending in n)

sentences.l: There, Waṅ-Qān's younger brothers, the nobles, and the others, while speaking together:
sentences.i: There the younger brothers of Wang Qan, the nobles and the rest, speaking together, said:
sentences.n: kiġed is glossed 等 'and so on': 'the younger brothers, the nobles and the others'. ügüleldürün is ügüle- 'speak' + the reciprocal -ldü- + the converb of time -rün; the speech that follows, introduced by the colon, runs on through the next twenty-two units and is closed by bida" in the unit beginning Ker kikün. Shiratori's quotation marks are printed with the words, so they appear in `t`.

sentences.t: "Ene qān aqa bidan-u ügeġü aburitu hümegei helige eburidčü jabuju.

morph.gloss: we (inclusive; stem bidan- before case endings) [咱的]
lacking, poor (Ming 窮), here perhaps 'wretched' [窮]
to hold in the bosom, harbour (stem uncertain) [懷着]
converb -žu written -ju, standing as a finite 'is going about' (uncertain; Ming 有 'is')

sentences.l: This Qan, elder brother, of us poor of temper, a foul liver, cherishing in the bosom, he goes about.
sentences.i: 'This Qan, our elder brother, goes about with a wretched temper and a foul liver in his bosom.
sentences.n: 'Foul liver' is the Ming 臭肝, and 'liver' is where the Mongols place feeling and kinship, so the phrase means a spiteful heart; it recurs below. ügeġü is the Ming 窮 'poor'; 'poor of temper' is the literal reading, and 'wretched' in the English is my sense for it, a guess. aburitu is aburi 'temper' + -tu 'having': a possessive in -tu is regularly 'having X', as in 'wife-having'. The Ming glosses jabuju 行有 'is going about'; the ending -ju is a puzzle (the converb -žu used as a finite verb), and I follow the Ming.

sentences.t: Aqa deġü-ji baraba;

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.l: The elder brother, the younger brother, has finished off;
sentences.i: The elder brother has finished off his younger brother;
sentences.n: A three-word clause closed by a semicolon. baraba is bara- 'be finished' + past, and the Ming gloss 了了 'finished' suggests an intransitive verb used with an accusative object, 'finished (him)'. The Ming 弟行 for deġü-ji marks the accusative with the same 行 it uses for the dative.

sentences.t: Qara-Kitad-tur ba oroba kü;

words.reading: 中合舌剌-乞(塔)惕-途舌兒 Qara-Kitad-tur

glyphs.s: 中合舌剌-乞(塔)惕-途舌兒

morph.gloss: indeed, just (emphatic particle; Ming 也) [也]

sentences.l: To the Qara-Kitad also he has gone in;
sentences.i: he has gone into the Qara-Kitad as well;
sentences.n: ba, here 'also', and kü, the emphatic 'indeed' glossed 也, flank the verb oroba. Taking ba and kü together as 'indeed also' is a guess; neither word carries much weight in the sense.

sentences.t: ulus ba žobaγ̇amu.

morph.gloss: people, realm, nation (Ming 百姓 'common people') [百姓]
to afflict, cause hardship (Ming 敎辛苦 'make toil'; stem uncertain) [敎辛苦有]

sentences.l: The people also he makes suffer.
sentences.i: and he makes the people suffer.
sentences.n: žobaγ̇amu is glossed 敎辛苦 'causing toil', which looks like a causative of žobaγ-; the exact stem is uncertain. ulus is 'people, realm', and the Ming 百姓 means the common folk.

sentences.t: Edöġe eġün-i ker kikün bida.

morph.gloss: this one (stem of ene before case endings) [這箇 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to do (the Ming gloss 怎飮 'how drink' cannot be the sense; the meaning is taken from the form) [怎飮]

sentences.l: Now this one how shall we do with?
sentences.i: Now, what are we to do with him?
sentences.n: ker kikün, 'how to do', is the Ming 怎生 怎飮. The Ming gloss for kikün reads 怎飮, with 飮 'drink', which cannot be the sense; the gloss may be a slip, and the meaning 'do' is taken from the form and the context. bida 'we' is the inclusive form, 'you and I together', and is marked 咱 in the Ming.

sentences.t: Erte üdür kēġesü
sentences.l: Formerly, day, if one speaks,
sentences.i: To speak of former days:
sentences.n: erte üdür, the Ming 在前 日子, means 'in the old days'. kēġesü is keġe- 'say' + -sü (conditional), 'if one says', written with a long vowel; it is an idiom for introducing a past matter and 'to speak of' is how I have put it.

sentences.t: doloγ̇an nasutu-ji Merkid irgen daγ̇uližu odču

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.l: Seven years of age-having the Merkid people, plundering, going,
sentences.i: When he was seven, the Merkid people plundered him and carried him off,
sentences.n: nasutu-ji is nasu 'age' + -tu 'having' + the accusative: 'the one having seven years' (the Ming 歲(有的)行). The Ming never names the boy but he is the object; Wang Qan's boyhood capture by the Merkid is the story. daγ̇uli- 'plunder' takes a person as its object in the Ming, as it does elsewhere.

sentences.t: qara alaγ ešige daqu emüsgežü

morph.gloss: sheep or goat, its hide (Ming 𦍩䍽; lamb or kid not shown) [𦍩䍽]
to make wear, put on (Ming 敎穿着; stem uncertain) [敎穿着]

sentences.l: A black mottled sheepskin fur-coat, having him wear,
sentences.i: made him wear a coat of black mottled sheepskin,
sentences.n: ešige is glossed 𦍩䍽, the same character as for imaγan in §151, which says only 'sheep or goat'; with the following daqu, Ming 皮襖 'skin coat', it gives 'sheepskin coat'. Whether ešige is a lamb, a kid or the grown animal the Ming does not say. emüsgežü is a converb of a verb whose stem I cannot pin down (emüs- 'wear' with a causative -ge- is likely); the Ming 敎穿着 'making wear' gives the sense.

sentences.t: Seleṅge-jin Buγ̇ura Keġer-e Merkid-ün aγ̇ur nödübe-kü.

morph.gloss: the Selenge, a river (Ming 河名) [河名 的]
Buγ̇ura, a place name (also 'stud camel') [地名]
open ground, steppe (Ming 野甸) [(野甸)行]
genitive: of (after a consonant, front-vowel form)
to pound (Ming 儔 'companion', perhaps a slip for 擣 'pound'; stem uncertain) [儔了 也]

sentences.l: The Selenge's Buγ̇ura steppe on, the Merkid's mortar, he pounded.
sentences.i: and he pounded at the Merkid's pestle-mill on the steppe at Buqura, by the Selenge.
sentences.n: aγ̇ur is glossed 碓 'a mortar worked by treading, a pestle mill'. nödübe-kü is the doubtful word: the Ming gloss 儔 'a companion' is not a verb of pounding. It may be a slip for 擣 'pound' (the two share the right-hand part 壽), which would suit 碓 beside it; that is only my conjecture, and I read the clause as the plain sense 'pounded at the mill' without being sure. Who set him to the work the text does not say. The Ming 地名 for Buγ̇ura says only 'a place name'; the same letters mean 'stud camel' elsewhere.

sentences.t: Qurčaqus-Buiruγ Qān ečige in-ü žiči Merkid irge qaγ̇ulžu köġü-ben tende aburažu ireġesü

words.reading: 中忽舌兒察中忽思-不亦舌魯黑 Qurčaqus-Buiruγ

glyphs.s: 中忽舌兒察中忽思-不亦舌魯黑

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person possessive, placed after its noun) [他的]
people (Ming 百姓; a form of irgen) [百姓]
to break, rout (Ming 破着; elsewhere 'rush') [破着]
son (short form of köġün) [兒子自的行]

sentences.l: Qurčaqus-Buiruγ Qān, father his, then the Merkid people, breaking, son-his there, rescuing, when he came,
sentences.i: Then his father Qurchaqus-Buiruq Qan routed the Merkid people and rescued his own son there, and came away.
sentences.n: in-ü is the third-person 'his', placed after its noun (ečige in-ü, 'father his'); köġü-ben is the reflexive possessive, 'his own son'. qaγ̇ulžu is glossed 破着 'breaking', 'routing'; elsewhere the same letters mean 'rush', so the meaning here is inferred. The unit holds a whole conditional chain, closed by ireġesü, 'when he came'; the English makes 'came away' the closing verb, since the conditional is left hanging into the next unit.

sentences.t: basa Tatar-un Ažai Qān harban γurban nasutu-ji eke selte basa daγ̇uližu odču

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
Ajai, a man's name (the Tatar ruler) [人名]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
with, bringing along (read from the Ming 連 'together with') [連]

sentences.l: Again, of the Tatars Ažai Qān, thirteen years of age-having, mother with, again, plundering, going,
sentences.i: Then Ajai Qan of the Tatars again plundered him, at thirteen, together with his mother, and carried them off,
sentences.n: Wang Qan is here an object of the plundering, not the subject: nasutu-ji is accusative again. selte, 'with', is a doubtful word that I read from the Ming 連 'together with'; it follows the same pattern as the previous capture. harban γurban is 'ten three', the Mongol way to say thirteen.

sentences.t: temeġed(i)-jen adulaγ̇ulun jabuqui-dur

morph.gloss: Shiratori's bracketed (i) before the reflexive (perhaps the accusative -i; Ming 行)
to herd, pasture (Ming 牧放) [敎牧放]

sentences.l: His own camels, causing to herd, at the going about,
sentences.i: and, as he was set to herding Ajai's own camels,
sentences.n: temeġed(i)-jen is the plural of temeġen 'camel', with a linking (i) and the reflexive -jen; the possessive 'his own' refers back to the master Ajai, not to the herder. adulaγ̇ulun is a causative: Ajai had him herd. jabuqui-dur is the participle 'going about' plus the dative-locative: 'at the going', that is 'while'.

sentences.t: Ažai Qān-u qoniči abuγ̇ad horγužu irebe že.

morph.gloss: indeed, so (particle; Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.l: Ažai Qān's shepherd, having taken, fleeing, he came indeed.
sentences.i: a shepherd of Ajai Qan took him and fled with him, and so he came away.
sentences.n: že, the Ming 也者, 'so, indeed', ends sentences in the narrative as a settling particle, and the English has no word for it. Who 'came' — the boy, taken by the shepherd — is carried by the Ming 逃着 来了, 'fleeing, he came'; the text does not make the shepherd's act of kindness or of theft clear.

sentences.t: Basa teġün-ü qoina Naiman-ača ajužu buruγ̇udču
sentences.l: Again, after that, from the Naiman, fearing, fleeing,
sentences.i: After that, afraid of the Naiman, he fled again,
sentences.n: Naiman-ača, with the ablative, is the cause: 'fearing from the Naiman'. aju- 'fear' and buruγ̇ud- are given as converbs and share a subject. basa, 'again', begins this as a new sequence.

sentences.t: Sartaγ̇ul-un γažar-a Čui müren-(n)e Qara-Kitad-un Gür Qān-dur odba že.

morph.gloss: the Muslims of Central Asia, Sarta'ul (Ming 囘囘) [囘囘的]
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
the Chu, a river (Ming 河名) [河名]
dative-locative: to, at (front-vowel form; the bracketed (n) is Shiratori's, the stem already ending in n)
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)

sentences.l: The Sartaγ̇ul's land to, the Chu river at, of the Qara-Kitad Gür Qān to, he went indeed.
sentences.i: to the land of the Sarta'ul, to the river Chu, to Gür Qan of the Qara-Kitad, he went.
sentences.n: Sartaγ̇ul is the Mongol name for the Muslim peoples of Central Asia, the Ming 囘囘. Three datives in a row — 'to the land, to the river, to Gür Qan' — are a list of where he went, from wide to narrow. This is the second time Wang Qan flees to Gür Qan; the first is in §151.

sentences.t: Tende nigen hon ülü daγ̇usun

morph.gloss: to bear, endure (stem uncertain; perhaps daγ̇us- 'be finished') [受]

sentences.l: There, one year, not enduring,
sentences.i: There he did not last even a year,
sentences.n: daγ̇usun, 'enduring', is the Ming 受 'receiving'; the stem is uncertain (daγ̇us- 'be finished' would give 'before a year was out'), but ülü, the negative that pairs with participles, tells us it means 'not enduring'. nigen hon, 'one year', stands before the negative in the Mongol order.

sentences.t: žiči daičin ködölžü Uiγ̇ud-un Taṅγ̇ud-un γažar(i)-jar bitužu jaburun jadažu

morph.gloss: to move, set in motion (stem inferred from the Ming 動着) [動着]
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)

words.reading: 中合札舌里-牙舌兒 γažar(i)-jar

morph.gloss: to go along (Ming 沿着) [沿着]

sentences.l: Then, rebellion setting in motion, the Uighurs', the Tangut's land through, along, while going, being in want,
sentences.i: then he set off in revolt, going along through the lands of the Uighurs and Tangut, in want,
sentences.n: daičin ködölžü, glossed 反 動着, is 'moving rebellion', much like bulγa bolun in the first section. γažar(i)-jar is γažar 'land' + (i) + -jar, the instrumental: 'through, by way of'. jaburun is jabu- + -run, 'while going'. Wang Qan is again the subject; the Ming lacks any marker.

sentences.t: tabun imaγ̇ad širgüġeležü saγ̇ažu temeġen-ü čisun qanažu idežü

morph.gloss: to hold fast, keep confined (stem uncertain) [拘着]

sentences.l: Five goats, holding fast, milking, of the camel blood piercing, eating,
sentences.i: holding five goats fast and milking them, pricking a camel's blood and drinking it,
sentences.n: This is the same formula as in §151 (imaγ̇ad širgüġeležü … temeġen-ü čisun qanažu ideġed) and the narrator repeats it deliberately: the second flight reproduces the first. Here saγ̇ažu, 'milking', is spelled plain, without the -du- of the earlier saγ̇al-dužu.

sentences.t: γaγča soqor qaliγ̇un moritu jadažu

morph.gloss: a horse colour (Ming 黑髮尾黃 'black mane, yellow tail'; sense uncertain) [黑髮尾黃]

sentences.l: A single, blind, black-maned yellow-tailed horse-having, being in want,
sentences.i: with a single blind horse, black-maned and yellow-tailed, being in want,
sentences.n: qaliγ̇un is glossed 黑髮尾黃 'black hair, yellow tail', but I do not know a horse-colour of that name and give the Ming's description 'black-maned, yellow-tailed' as it stands; it may be a loose gloss. moritu is mori 'horse' + -tu: 'horse-having'. soqor is one-eyed or blind.

sentences.t: Temüžin köġün-dür ireġesü qubčir-i qubčižu težiġebe že.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name (Chinggis's birth name) [(人)名]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.l: To Temüžin the son, when he came, a levy levying, he reared indeed.
sentences.i: he came to his son Temüjin, who collected a levy and fed him.
sentences.n: köġün-dür, 'to the son', with the Ming 兒行: the brothers, speaking of Wang Qan, call Temüjin his 'son' (the Ming 兒行). The levy and the feeding repeat the language of §151, with the same -ġesü, 'when he came'. že, 'indeed', again closes the retelling.

sentences.t: Edöġe Temüžin köġün-dür tein jabuγsan(i)-jan umartažu hümegei helige ebüridčü jabumu.

morph.gloss: to walk, go about, act [行了的 自的行]
Shiratori's bracketed (i) before the reflexive (perhaps the accusative -i; Ming 行)
to hold in the bosom, harbour (stem uncertain) [懷着]

sentences.l: Now, to Temüžin the son, so having acted-his-own, forgetting, a foul liver, harbouring, he goes about.
sentences.i: Now, forgetting how he treated his son Temüjin, he goes about harbouring a foul liver.
sentences.n: jabuγsan(i)-jan: the participle 'having acted', Shiratori's bracketed (i) (perhaps the accusative: the Ming 行 marks it as the object of 'forgetting'), and the reflexive -jan ('his own conduct'). The Ming 忘了着 gives 'forgetting', and the clause is a reproach by Wang Qan's own brothers. The 'foul liver' repeats the phrase of the first speech.

sentences.t: Ker kikün bida" keġeldübe.
sentences.l: How shall we do, we, they said together.
sentences.i: What are we to do?' they said to one another.
sentences.n: The closing quotation mark is printed on bida"; it ends the speech that began at "Ene qān aqa. keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- + past: 'said together'.

sentences.t: Ein ügüledügsen üges-i Altun-Asuγ Waṅ-Qān-(n)a siqaγlažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
dative-locative: to, at (back-vowel form; the bracketed (n) is Shiratori's, the stem already ending in n)

words.reading: 阿亦中合黑剌主兀 siqaγlažuγ̇u

morph.gloss: to inform on, denounce (Ming 訐吿) [訐吿了]

sentences.l: Thus the said words, Altun-Asuγ to Waṅ-Qān informed on.
sentences.i: Altun-Asuq informed Wang Qan of the words they had spoken together.
sentences.n: üges-i: the word üge 'speech', the plural -s, and the accusative -i; the Ming 言語每(行) is the same. siqaγlažuγ̇u is glossed 訐吿 'inform against'. Shiratori prints ügüledügsen without the l that the Han 勒 supplies (ügüle-ldü-gsen). The tense -žuγ̇u is the narrative past, as in orožuγ̇ui earlier.

sentences.t: Altun-Asuγ ügü- lerün:

morph.gloss: to speak, first half of ügü-lerün split at the line end [說]
converb of time: saying (the Ming gives no gloss for this token)

sentences.l: Altun-Asuγ, while saying:
sentences.i: Altun-Asuq said:
sentences.n: ügü- and lerün are one word, ügülerün 'while saying', broken by the line end into two tokens. The Ming gives no gloss for the second half, 246 being empty.

sentences.t: "Bi ber ene eje-dür oroldulaγ̇a-kü;

morph.gloss: counsel, plan (Ming 商量 'deliberation'; usually eje means 'master, lord') [商量裏]

words.reading: 斡舌羅勒都︀剌阿-古 oroldulaγ̇a-kü

sentences.l: I also this counsel into have entered together;
sentences.i: 'I also entered into this plan;
sentences.n: eje-dür is glossed 商量裏 'in the counsel'. The ordinary meaning of eje is 'master, lord', and I take it as a different sense here, from the Ming. oroldulaγ̇a-kü is oro- + the reciprocal -ldu- + a past + kü: 'went in together', that is, took part.

sentences.t: žiči Qān(i)-jan čima-ji tebčin jadaba" keġežü

morph.gloss: the accusative -i, 'one's own qan (object)', Shiratori's bracketed vowel before the reflexive
reflexive possessive: one's own (here the speaker's, 'my own'; back-vowel form)
you (oblique stem čima- before the accusative) [你行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.l: But my own Qan, you giving up, I could not, saying,
sentences.i: but, my own Qan, I could not abandon you,' he said.
sentences.n: čima-ji is 'you' in the accusative on the oblique stem čima-. tebčin jadaba, 'giving up, could not', is the Ming 捨 不能了. keġežü closes the quotation, Shiratori's quotation mark printed on jadaba".

sentences.t: tende Waṅ-Qān ein ügüleldügsed El-Qutur, Qulbari, Arin-Taiži-tan deġü-ner(i)-jen nojad(i)-jan bariγ̇ulžuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 嗚詁列勒都︀克薛惕 ügüleldügsed

morph.gloss: past participle, plural: those who had …
Shiratori's bracketed (i) before the reflexive (perhaps the accusative -i; Ming 行)
noble, lord [官人每 自的行]
Shiratori's bracketed (i) before the reflexive (perhaps the accusative -i; Ming 行)
to seize, take hold of [敎拿了有來]

sentences.l: There Waṅ-Qān, thus those who had spoken together, El-Qutur, Qulbari, Arin-Taiži and the like, his younger brothers, his nobles, had seized.
sentences.i: There Wang Qan had his brothers and nobles who had spoken so seized: El-Qutur, Qulbari, Arin-Taiji and the rest.
sentences.n: -tan on Arin-Taiži is the Ming 等 'and so on', glossing a list of names. deġü-ner(i)-jen and nojad(i)-jan have linking (i) and the reflexive 'his own', each in its own vowel-harmony form: -jen after front-vowel deġü-ner, -jan after back-vowel nojad; in both the (i) is Shiratori's bracketed vowel, perhaps the accusative (the Ming 行 marks the objects). The sentence ends with bariγ̇ulžuγ̇ui, a causative (bari- 'seize' + -γ̇ul-).

sentences.t: Deġü-ner-e- če Žaqaγambu buruγ̇udču Naiman-dur orožuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: first half of the ablative -eče, split at the line end
ablative: from, second half of deġü-ner-e-če, split at the line end [內]
to hide, flee (stem uncertain) [逃躱了着]

sentences.l: Of the younger brothers, Žaqaγambu, fleeing, to the Naiman, went in.
sentences.i: Of the brothers, Jaqagambu fled and went in to the Naiman.
sentences.n: Deġü-ner-e- and če are one word, the ablative deġü-nere-če 'from among the younger brothers', broken at the line end. Jaqa Gambu is glossed only 人名; the 'among the brothers' makes him one of Wang Qan's. The ablative here is partitive, 'out of the brothers'.

sentences.t: Teden-i bariγ̇as selte ger-tür oroγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: accusative on the oblique stem teden-
shackles, restraints (Ming 刑禁; from bari- 'to seize') [刑禁]

sentences.l: Those, in shackles with, into the tent, making enter,
sentences.i: They were brought, in shackles, into the tent,
sentences.n: bariγ̇as, glossed 刑禁 'penal restraint', is my 'shackles'. The accusative on teden-i is the oblique stem teden- + -i. oroγ̇ulžu is oro- 'enter' + the causative: 'bringing in'; its subject is Wang Qan, named in the next unit.

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān, while saying:
sentences.i: and Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: A two-word unit, kept short because it introduces the long speech to come. ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün, the same converb of time.

sentences.t: "Bida Uiγ̇ud-un Taṅγ̇ud-un γažar(i)-jar aisuqui-dur jaγ̇u keġeldüleġei;

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)
genitive: of (after a consonant, back-vowel form)

words.reading: 中合札舌里-牙舌兒 γažar(i)-jar
阿亦速(中灰)-突︀舌兒 aisuqui-dur

sentences.l: We, the Uighurs', the Tangut's land through, when coming, what we said together;
sentences.i: 'When we were coming through the lands of the Uighurs and Tangut, what did we say to one another?
sentences.n: Wang Qan reminds the prisoners of what they said to one another on the road through the Uighur and Tangut lands. keġeldüleġei is keġe- + reciprocal + past -leġei (Ming 來). The Uighurs and Tangut appear here as in the first section.

sentences.t: tan-u metü jaγ̇u sedkikü bi"

morph.gloss: you (plural; stem tan- before case endings) [您(的)]

sentences.l: Like you, what shall I think, I,
sentences.i: How should I think as you do?'
sentences.n: tan-u metü, 'like yours', and jaγ̇u sedkikü bi, 'what shall I think'. The Ming 您的般甚麽想我 gives only the word-order of the sentence, not a sense, and I read it as a rhetorical question — 'would I think as you think?' — but the line is obscure and I may be wrong.

sentences.t: kēġed niγ̇ur-tür an-u nilbužu bariγ̇as an-u tabiγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: on, to (front-vowel form, printed after a back-vowel stem)
their, his (third-person possessive, back-vowel counterpart of in-ü; placed after its noun) [他的]
to let go, set loose [放了]

sentences.l: Having said, on their faces spitting, their shackles, he released.
sentences.i: So saying, he spat in their faces and had their shackles taken off.
sentences.n: nilbužu is nilbu- 'spit'. Putting an-u after its noun, as in 'faces their', is the third-person possessive, as in-ü earlier. tabiγ̇ulba is tabi- 'let go' + the causative: 'made loose'.

sentences.t: Qān-a ele nilbuγdažu ger-tür bükün haran büġüdeġer bosču nilbužuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: only, just (emphatic particle; Ming 但) [但]

sentences.l: By the Qan only, being spat upon, in the tent being, the people all, rising, they spat.
sentences.i: As soon as Wang Qan had spat on them, all the people in the tent rose and spat on them too.
sentences.n: Qān-a with the dative and a passive, nilbuγdažu, gives 'being spat upon by the Qan' — the dative names who does the spitting, as the -da on aqa-daγ̇an did. ele is the Ming 但, 'only' or, in the Chinese of the time, 'as soon as'; I take the second sense, which the English follows, but it is a guess. büġüde-ġer: büġüde 'all' with an instrumental -ġer, used as an adverb. The paragraph's last verb, nilbužuγ̇ui, is the narrative past.

sentences.t: Tere übül übülžežü noγai žil namur in-ü

morph.gloss: his, its (third-person possessive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: That winter, having wintered, dog year, autumn, its,
sentences.i: After spending that winter, in the autumn of the Dog year,
sentences.n: noγai žil, 'dog year', is the Mongol twelve-year cycle; the Dog year is conventionally dated 1202, but the text itself gives no Western year. in-ü after namur, 'autumn its', is the third-person 'its', the autumn belonging to the year. The Ming 他的 marks it.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Čaγ̇aγ̇an-Tatar, Alči-Tatar, Dutaγ̇ud, Alγai-Tatar tede Tatar-tur

morph.gloss: the Duta'ud, a Tatar group [種(名)]

words.reading: 阿魯中孩-塔塔舌兒 Alγai-Tatar

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, the Čaγ̇aγ̇an Tatar, the Alči Tatar, the Dutaγ̇ud, the Alγai Tatar, those Tatars against,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, against those Tatars, the Chagan Tatars, the Alchi Tatars, the Duta'ud and the Alqai Tatars,
sentences.n: Four Tatar groups are named in a row and then summed up by tede Tatar-tur, 'those Tatars to' (dative). čaγ̇aγ̇an is 'white'; the Ming 種(名) says only 'name of a people'. The sentence has no verb yet; it is held open through the next unit.

sentences.t: Dalan-Nemürges baildužu qadqul- duqui-jin urida

words.reading: 荅闌-捏木舌兒格思 Dalan-Nemürges

morph.gloss: Dalan-Nemürges, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名]
to fight, clash (Ming 厮殺) [厮殺︀]

sentences.l: Dalan-Nemürges at, standing against each other, of the fighting, before,
sentences.i: standing in array at Dalan-Nemürges, before the fighting,
sentences.n: baildužu is bai- 'stand' + the reciprocal -ldu- + -žu: 'standing facing each other', the Ming 對陣着. qadqul-duqui-jin is split by the line end and shows the participle -qui with a genitive: 'of the clashing'. urida, 'before', then governs the genitive.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žasaγ ügüleldürün:

morph.gloss: law, regulation, military discipline (Ming 軍法) [軍法]

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, the law, while speaking together:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan laid down the law, saying:
sentences.n: žasaγ means 'law, regulation' here; the Ming glosses 軍法, 'military law'. ügüleldürün is the same converb as in the earlier introductions to speech, and what follows is a rule, not a conversation.

sentences.t: "Daisun küġü daruγ̇asu olža-dur bu baija,

morph.gloss: to press down, overcome (also written dara-) [勝了呵]

sentences.l: The enemy men, if we overcome them, on the spoil, let us not stand,
sentences.i: 'If we defeat the enemy, let us not stop for the spoil;
sentences.n: daruγ̇asu is daru- 'press down, overcome' + the conditional -γasu: 'if we overcome' (the vowel u shows the stem is daru-, not dara-). bu baija is the prohibitive bu with the hortative -ja: 'let us not halt'. olža-dur is olža 'spoil' with the dative-locative. The Ming 休立咱 reads literally 'don't stand, we'.

sentences.t: darun baraγ̇asu tere olža bidan-uγ̇ai bi-že.

morph.gloss: to press down, overcome (also written dara-) [勝]

sentences.l: Overcoming, when we have finished, that spoil, ours it is indeed.
sentences.i: when we have finished them, that spoil will be ours.
sentences.n: darun baraγ̇asu: daru- + a converb, then bara- 'to finish' used as a helper, and the conditional -γasu. bidan-uγ̇ai is the genitive of bida with an ending I cannot name for certain; the Ming 咱的 gives 'ours'. bi-že, 'is indeed', is the Ming 有也者.

sentences.t: Qubijaldud-že bida.

words.reading: 中忽必牙勒都︀惕-者︀ Qubijaldud-že

morph.gloss: to divide, share (Ming 分) [共分 也者︀]

sentences.l: Let us share it out, we.
sentences.i: Let us share it out among ourselves.
sentences.n: Qubijaldud-že is qubi- 'divide' with the reciprocal -ldu- and a -d that I cannot parse exactly; the Ming 共分也者 gives 'divide together, indeed'. bida closes the sentence; the quotation goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: Nögör küġün-e ičuγ̇aγdaγ̇asu türün-ü dobtuluγsan γažar-tur(i)-jan egeġerüje

morph.gloss: companion, but the Ming glosses 被敵 'by the enemy' (reading uncertain) [被敵]
to drive back, repel (Ming 趕退) [趕退呵]
first, at first (Ming 始初 'at the beginning') [始初的]

words.reading: 中合札舌兒-都︀舌里-顏 γažar-tur(i)-jan

morph.gloss: land, place [地面 裏自的行]
to turn back (Ming 翻身 'turn the body') [翻身咱]

sentences.l: By the foe-man if we are driven back, of the first, the charged place to, let us turn back;
sentences.i: If the enemy drives us back, let us turn about to our own place of the first charge;
sentences.n: nögör normally means 'companion', which gives the wrong sense; the Ming 被敵 'by the enemy' makes me read it as 'foe' here, but this is uncertain. ičuγ̇aγdaγ̇asu is ičuγ̇a- 'drive back' + passive + the conditional. egeġerüje is 'let us turn back' (the Ming 翻身咱, literally 'turn the body').

sentences.t: türün-ü dubtulγan-dur ese egeġerügsen küġün-i mököriġülüje"

words.reading: 多卜禿勒中罕-突︀舌兒 dubtulγan-dur

morph.gloss: to charge, attack (a spelling of dobtul-) [衝的 時裏]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to cut down, behead (Ming 斬了; stem uncertain) [斬了者︀咱]

sentences.l: Of the first, at the charge, not having turned, the man, let us have cut down,
sentences.i: whoever did not turn back at the first charge, let us have him cut down,'
sentences.n: The rule is stated twice, positive then negative. ese before the participle egeġerügsen is the past negative 'not having turned'. mököriġülüje is a causative, 'let us cause (him) to be cut down'; the stem mököri- is uncertain.

sentences.t: keġen žasaγlalduba.
sentences.l: Saying, they agreed the law together.
sentences.i: So they agreed on the rule.
sentences.n: keġen closes the quotation; žasaγlalduba is žasaγ 'law', the verb-maker -la-, the reciprocal -ldu-, and the past -ba: 'ruled together', 'settled the regulation among them'.

sentences.t: Dalan-Nemürges qadquldužu Tatar-i ködölgebe.

words.reading: 荅闌-捏木舌兒格思 Dalan-Nemürges
中合(惕)中忽勒都︀周 qadquldužu

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to move, set in motion (Ming 推動) [推動了]

sentences.l: Dalan-Nemürges, fighting each other, the Tatars he set in motion.
sentences.i: At Dalan-Nemürges they fought, and drove the Tatars back.
sentences.n: ködölgebe is ködöl- 'move' + the causative -ge-: 'made move', and the Ming 推動了 means 'pushed out of place'. Tatar-i is the accusative, 'the Tatars (object)'.

sentences.t: Daružu Ulqui Šilügelžid- te ulus-tur an-u neileġülüž daγ̇uliba.

morph.gloss: to press down, overcome (also written dara-) [勝着]
the Ulqui, a river (Ming 河名) [河(名)]
Shilügeljid, a place name (Ming 地名; the word is split at the line end) [(地)名]
dative-locative: at (after d, a form of -de) [行]
to unite, join together (Ming 相合) [相合着]

sentences.l: Overcoming, at Ulqui Šilügelžid, in the realm, their, uniting, he seized.
sentences.i: Following up the victory, at Shilügeljid by the Ulqui, he gathered their people together and seized them.
sentences.n: Šilügelžid- and -te are one word, the place name with the locative, split at the line end. neileġülüž is neile- 'unite' + causative + a converb in -ž, which is how the text prints it. The Ming reads the clause as 'joining their (people) together, seizing', and I follow it; the grammar is not secure.

sentences.t: Čaγan-Tatar, Alči-Tatar, Dutaγ̇ud-Tatar, Alγai-Tatar erkid irge tende muqudγažu

words.reading: 都︀塔兀惕-塔塔舌兒 Dutaγ̇ud-Tatar

morph.gloss: the Duta'ud, a Tatar group [種(名)]

words.reading: 阿魯中孩-塔塔舌兒 Alγai-Tatar

morph.gloss: to wipe out, destroy (Ming 絕 'cut off') [絕着]

sentences.l: The Čaγan Tatars, the Alči Tatars, the Dutaγ̇ud Tatars, the Alγai Tatars, the important people, there, wiping out,
sentences.i: destroying there the leading people of the Chagan Tatars, the Alchi Tatars, the Duta'ud Tatars and the Alqai Tatars,
sentences.n: erkid is erke 'power' with the plural -d; the Ming 緊要每 means 'the important ones', and so 'leading people'. muqudγažu is glossed 絕 'cut off'; the stem is likely muqudγa- 'destroy, make an end of'.

sentences.t: žasaγ ügüledügsen üġes-tür Altan, Qučar, Daritai
sentences.l: The law, in the spoken words, Altan, Qučar, Daritai,
sentences.i: As to the words of the law that had been spoken: Altan, Quchar and Daritai,
sentences.n: üġes-tür is üge 'word' + the plural -s + the dative-locative: 'in the words'. The three names are the Ming 人名, and they are three named men; the grammar waits for a verb until the next unit.

sentences.t: γurban ügeš-tür ülü kürün olža-dur baižuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: to stand, to stop [立了有來]

sentences.l: The three, in the word not reaching, on the spoil, stood.
sentences.i: the three of them did not keep to the word, and stopped for the spoil.
sentences.n: ülü kürün, 'not reaching', with üge, 'to the word', is an idiom for not obeying; the Ming 不到 言語每 裏 is the literal 'not arriving at the words'. baižuγ̇ui is bai- 'stand' + the perfect: 'has stood', 'stopped'. The plural is written ügeš-tür here with š, and üġes-tür above; the spelling wavers in Shiratori.

sentences.t: Üġes-tür ese kürbe keġen
sentences.l: To the word not it reached, saying,
sentences.i: 'They did not keep to the word,' he said,
sentences.n: kürbe is the plain past of kür-, 'arrive'. keġen closes the quotation, as before. The unit is a quoted verdict, short, kept apart from the sentence it hangs on.

sentences.t: Žebe, Qubilai qojar-i iležü

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.l: Žebe, Qubilai, the two, sending,
sentences.i: and sent the two, Jebe and Qubilai,
sentences.n: Jebe and Qubilai are named without a title. qojar-i is the accusative 'the two', which is why they are the object of ile-, 'to send'. The Ming 走去着 on iležü is 'going', but since Chinggis is the doer, I read 'sending'.

sentences.t: olžalaγsad aduγ̇un jaγ̇u-ge abuγsad-i bügüde-ji abqaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: past participle, plural: those who had …
past participle, plural: those who had taken
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.l: The ones who took spoil, livestock, whatever, of those who had taken, all, made to be taken.
sentences.i: to take back from everyone who had seized spoil whatever livestock they had taken.
sentences.n: olžalaγsad is olža 'spoil' + -la- + a participle in the plural, 'those who had taken spoil'. abuγsad-i is the same, 'the ones who had taken', in the accusative. abqaγ̇ulba is ab- 'take' + the causative -qaγ̇ul-: 'caused to be taken (back)'. The Ming 敎要了 supports a causative. The last sentence of the section ends on this verb.
